findings.title: Hidden check walks unbounded ancestors
findings.message: The loop walks up through all ancestors, including the toolbar and beyond. If any ancestor carries the hidden property, then the record is reported as hidden. Also, node.AsTree().Parent may be a typed nil, but tree.IsNil handles that. The behavior change makes non-group toolbar items inherit hidden state from any ancestor, which could affect unrelated widgets.
findings.suggestion: Limit the walk to ancestors that are within the same overflow toolbar, stopping at the toolbar owner.

findings.title: Depth limit off-by-one
findings.message: The depth check fires once len(visited) reaches 16, so a chain with exactly 16 ancestors (depth 16) is rejected, contradicting the documented depth of 16. The ancestry walk is also repeated for every item on every propose/View call, which is O(n*depth) and fine at 256 items but does redundant work.
findings.suggestion: Use len(visited) > 16 or document the limit as 15 ancestors.

finding.title: Expand accepted for items without children
finding.message: The expand event is proposed for a disabled item with disabled children, and Disabled is checked for ancestors but a disabled item cannot be collapsed. More importantly, ModelBrowserExpand on a leaf or item without children is accepted if called directly; stale callbacks for items that no longer have children are not refused.
finding.suggestion: For ModelBrowserExpand, verify the item still has children before calling Change.
